defects.description: Description: bend the arms slightly with one hand touching the wrist of the other, one arm raised overhead touching the wall. L arm correctly overhead (L wrist y=1.341, above head y=0.913, touching wall z=0.221). But R wrist at y=0.306 (at-side). L-wrist to R-wrist 3D distance 1.54 — hands far apart, no touching. The non-overhead arm (R) must reach UP to the overhead wrist.

Description says ONE arm raised overhead, but for R hand to touch L wrist (y=1.341, well above head y=0.913), R arm must also be raised significantly — rig constraint (max R wrist y = R shoulder y + upper_arm_len + forearm_len = 0.675+0.41+0.34 = 1.425). Partial fix only; full contact requires R arm near-overhead which conflicts with one-arm-overhead language.

failing_tests.assertion: L wrist to R wrist dist3D < 0.20 for hand-touching-wrist
R wrist y > 1.0 (approaching L wrist y=1.341)

regression_risk: medium — rightShoulder=-75 is large magnitude approaching PR-v4 overshoot territory (-110). Visual verification essential. If R arm appears too close to overhead, integrator may revert and accept contact failure as rig limit.
rationale: Partial fix to bring R hand closer to L wrist without making R arm fully overhead (would conflict with one-arm-overhead). (1) rightShoulder -40→-75: raise R upper arm from ~63deg abduction to ~110deg (upper arm past horizontal, pointing up-and-out). (2) rightElbow 60→70: slight increase in flexion so R forearm angles upward. Even with these changes R wrist unlikely to fully reach L wrist (1.341) due to limb-length geometry — rig limit acknowledged. Spine=-12 (PR-v3 fix), L arm overhead, globalTilt=5, hipAbductR=-15 (R leg crossing) all preserved. shoulderFwdR=8 unchanged.
